transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-22 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Mark Hamilton (CTO, Parallax), Priya Desai (Staff ML Eng), Evan Lee (Platform Eng)

Summary (auto): initial integration discovery focused on SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex usage patterns, gateway/proxy requirements, rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks. Discussed Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options and security needs (VPC/KMS/SOC2). Agreed to run a PoC perf benchmark and exchange security docs.

00:00:05 - Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Samir from Redwood, and with me is Lena our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
00:00:12 - Mark: good thanks, excited to chat. quick note, our timezone's est but we can run through everything.
00:00:18 - Lena: great - wanted to start with a quick overview of what you guys are trying to build and where inference fits into your stack.
00:00:24 - Priya: sure, so Parallax is building a contextual support assistant for our enterprise clients. we ingest docs, product data, and the assistant surfaces step-by-step actions. currently using in-house embeddings and an external API for generation, but costs and latency are getting out of hand at scale.
00:00:38 - Evan: and we need tighter controls around data residency and audit logs, plus SSO for our internal users.
00:00:44 - Samir: got it. are you already using any of the LLM dev stacks, like LangChain or LlamaIndex?
00:00:49 - Priya: we prototyped with LangChain and have a custom LlamaIndex layer for retrieval. we want to keep those libs in place, not rip them out.
00:00:56 - Lena: that's a common pattern. Redwood's SDKs are drop-in friendly - we have a Python SDK and a Node client and also a LangChain connector that most customers use. small caveat: sometimes names in our SDKs get mis-typed in docs, you'll see older references to "Redwood Serve" in one doc but the connector is in the SDK package.
00:01:10 - Mark: can you speak to the gateway setup? we have an internal gateway/proxy that handles auth and routing to multiple cloud services. we need to know if Redwood can sit behind our gateway or if we have to use a direct outbound connection.
00:01:22 - Lena: yes, you can run requests through your gateway. for Hosted API we recommend TLS mutual auth where possible and IP allowlisting. for Private/VPC deployments it's typically direct peering. we also support an on-prem proxy that can be deployed in front of the inference nodes for additional controls.
00:01:36 - Evan: and rate limiting? we have per-tenant quotas and bursty traffic. need to enforce per-tenant rate limits upstream and ideally have Redwood honor x-api-key scopes or similar.
00:01:45 - Samir: we have multi-tenant token-level quotas in the Hosted product; you can set per-api-key rate limits and daily quotas. Dedicated gives you more headroom and you can implement rate limiting at the gateway so Redwood isn't enforcing business tenant logic unless you want it to.
00:01:58 - Priya: latency: our SLO is p95 < 400ms for 512-token responses. curious if that's realistic on Hosted or if we need Dedicated.
00:02:06 - Lena: depends on traffic distribution. Hosted typically hits ~200-600ms for smaller models and shorter payloads; for consistent p95 under 400ms at heavy throughput we usually recommend Dedicated with pinned capacity. we can run a benchmark using your prompt mix and tokens; that'll tell us whether Hosted suffices.
00:02:22 - Mark: what about quantization and model choices - are you running open models, and do we get a say in model variants?
00:02:27 - Samir: yes, we provide a model catalog with curated open models and verified performance profiles. on Dedicated/Private you can pin model variants and choose quantization profiles. we also do automatic fallback to smaller variants if capacity constraints occur, but for sensitive workloads you can lock rollouts.
00:02:40 - Evan: observability hooks - what do you export? we need tracing, per-request tokens, cost attribution, and the ability to tie requests back to our internal trace ids.
00:02:49 - Lena: we export per-request telemetry including request id, model, token counts, latency breakdowns, and can inject your trace id if you pass it in a header. Console provides route-level dashboards, and you can enable higher retention for logs on Dedicated/Private.
00:03:02 - Priya: do you have a LangChain example for streaming responses and function calls? streaming is important for perceived latency.
00:03:09 - Lena: yes, our LangChain connector supports streaming and function/tool calling. there's a sample repo link in the deck - I'll share it in Slack. small heads-up: sometimes the function call semantics show up slightly different in older LangChain versions so we recommend LangChain >= 0.1x (note: version numbers mis-transcribed in a few docs).
00:03:26 - Mark: security - SOC2, KMS, SSO, RBAC - what's supported? we need to present to compliance.
00:03:33 - Samir: Hosted is SOC2 compliant for data at rest and in transit, we support customer-managed keys via KMS for Dedicated/Private, SAML SSO and RBAC through the Console. we'll send the SOC2 report and security deck after this call.
00:03:45 - Evan: for Private VPC/on-prem we need audit logs to be forwarded to our SIEM; can you do that?
00:03:50 - Lena: yes, log forwarding and webhook hooks are supported; for on-prem deployment logs stay inside your network.
00:03:55 - Priya: integration specifics - do you have rate-limit headers or quota endpoints so we can programmatically pull remaining quota?
00:04:01 - Samir: Hosted returns X-RateLimit-Remaining headers and has endpoints for quota status. For Dedicated we can provide custom quota endpoints integrated with your OIDC if needed.
00:04:11 - Mark: about the SDKs - what's the recommended deployment for backend services? we run services in k8s.
00:04:16 - Lena: run the SDK in your backend. for k8s we recommend a small proxy sidecar that handles retries, idempotency keys, and batching for high-throughput patterns. Redwood also offers a client-side batching library but many platform teams prefer the proxy approach.
00:04:29 - Evan: any examples with LlamaIndex? we have an indexer pipeline that writes to s3 and builds payloads.
00:04:34 - Lena: we have a LlamaIndex connector sample and a recommended pattern: do indexing offline, store embeddings in your vector DB, and call Redwood for generation. we'll share the LlamaIndex example link.
00:04:43 - Priya: ok, about pricing - if we go Dedicated what are the commit terms and burst policies?
00:04:48 - Samir: Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits. you get burst credits and configurable autoscaling policies. I'll include SKUs in the pricing deck but typical patterns are X GPUs reserved with burst pool.
00:04:58 - Mark: any hard limits for token sizes or sequence lengths? we have some long context docs sometimes >8k tokens.
00:05:03 - Lena: we support longer context lengths depending on the model. there are per-model limits; for very long contexts we recommend retrieval + chunking or a KV cache approach. cache can also reduce cost for repeated prefixes.
00:05:13 - Priya: what about telemetry cost attribution? can we get token-level billing per-team?
00:05:17 - Samir: yes, Console provides token-level cost by API key/route and you can export detailed usage CSVs for billing.
00:05:24 - [brief crosstalk]
00:05:30 - Evan: latency testing - what do you need from us to run the PoC?
00:05:33 - Lena: a sample workload: typical prompts, payload sizes, concurrency profile, and a test harness (we can provide a JMeter/script). Also any network topology constraints (eg, egress IPs).
00:05:44 - Priya: we can produce that by tomorrow.
00:05:46 - Samir: great. I'll also note that if you need end-to-end tracing we can patch trace ids through our system.
00:05:51 - Mark: one more Q - what's the path for Private on-prem? timeline and support?
00:05:55 - Lena: Private typically involves our control plane in your VPC and an on-prem inference cluster; timeline can be 6-12 weeks depending on compliance needs. for air-gapped on-prem it's longer. we'll scope this in the next meeting.
00:06:06 - Priya: any red flags from our side?
00:06:08 - Samir: no red flags, just a few clarifications: confirm token volumes, confirm whether you need customer-managed KMS, and decide if you want Redwood to do tenant-level quotas or keep that in your gateway.
00:06:17 - Mark: understood.
00:06:20 - [15 minute mark summary omitted for brevity; conversation continued on SDK nuances, sample payloads]
00:22:10 - Lena: one implementation nit - if you're doing batch embedding calls, we recommend doing batching client-side to reduce per-call overhead; we can give you a batching helper snippet.
00:22:22 - Priya: yes we batch, but sometimes the interactive flows need low latency so we mix streaming and small batch calls.
00:22:30 - Samir: that's expected. for mixed workloads Dedicated with autoscaling or Hosted with a caching layer can work.
00:22:37 - Evan: curious on observability retention - how long does Console keep detailed traces on Hosted?
00:22:41 - Lena: default retention is 30 days for detailed traces; Dedicated/Private can be configured to 90/365 days depending on the add-on.
00:22:49 - Priya: are there cost calculators?
00:22:51 - Samir: we'll attach a cost model spreadsheet; it takes inputs like tokens/day, model choice, and returns estimated monthly cost.
00:22:58 - Mark: competition - do customers switch from OpenAI or Anthropic often? any migration gotchas?
00:23:05 - Samir: yes, migration is common; main gotchas are prompt tuning and model differences. our eval tooling helps detect quality regressions. also watch for embedding vector drift when moving embedding providers.
00:23:17 - [small laugh]
00:23:20 - Evan: final logistics - can we get a network diagram and SOC2 now?
00:23:24 - Samir: yes, we'll send SOC2, security deck, and network peering doc after this call.
00:23:29 - Priya: great.
00:23:32 - Samir: to recap: we'll send pricing + Dedicated SKU, security docs, perf benchmark template. Parallax will send traffic profile and test harness. we'll schedule a follow-up demo Oct 29 to go deep into LangChain/LlamaIndex integration and run initial benchmark.
00:23:50 - Mark: that works. thanks everyone.
00:23:53 - Lena: thanks, we'll follow up with links and action items.
00:24:00 - [call ends]
